info.title: MCP Gateway Token Exchange
info.description: An MCP Gateway that fronts a self-hosted MCP server exposing a single `echo` tool. The gateway authenticates callers via Auth0 browser login (`mcp-auth0-oauth-inbound`), performs a real per-user OAuth token exchange to call the upstream MCP server with a token scoped to that upstream (`mcp-token-exchange-inbound`), and gates the `echo` tool behind an `echo` role (`mcp-capability-filter-inbound`). The upstream MCP server calls the downstream echo service using its own service-to-service credentials (`upstream-oauth-client-credentials-inbound`).

post.description: Forwards to Zuplo's public echo/reflector service (https://echo.zuplo.io), which echoes back the request it received — including whatever `Authorization` header was attached. Used as the MCP `echo` tool; this is also the hop the Auth0 token exchange happens on, so the exchanged token is visible in the reflected `headers.authorization` of the response.

200.description: The reflected request, as returned by echo.zuplo.io

get.description: Protected Resource Metadata (RFC 9728) for the upstream MCP server at /internal/echo/mcp. McpGatewayPlugin serves this document at the conventional well-known path for the routes it manages directly (the client-facing /mcp route); this same-project upstream publishes its own copy here instead, at a project-specific path, so echo-mcp-token-exchange's protectedResourceMetadataUrl option has a document to fetch for it.

post.description: The MCP server exposing the `echo` tool: translates a `tools/call` for `echo` into the `/echo` API call, which forwards to https://echo.zuplo.io. It's a genuine OAuth-protected upstream, with its own Auth0 audience, so the gateway's `mcp-token-exchange-inbound` policy on `/mcp` has a real per-user credential relationship to broker.

get,post.description: Public entry point for MCP clients. Authenticates the caller via Auth0 browser login, performs a real per-user OAuth token exchange for the upstream echo MCP server, and only exposes/allows the `echo` tool to callers whose `roles` claim includes `echo`.

tags.name: Echo
tags.description: Endpoints backing the echo MCP tool, its upstream MCP server, and the gateway that fronts it.
